Honestly, names seem a bit random in this game. If you use advanced weapons, it seems like it keeps the names short though.

For me, not having to compete with other players for rewards is a great design feature. In other MMOs, seeing another player often means it will be harder for me to get the items I want, but in this game, everyone gets credit or rewards on an individual basis. Another player is a good sign because they'll only be helping.

Although there are no mounts, this game uses a waypoint system which means you can go anywhere you've already been in seconds. It's a great system.

The end game content focuses on fashion rather than stats. It's very easy to get top-level armor that is good enough for any open-world PvE area. You'll have to put in a bit more work if you are looking to do raids or high-level dungeons, but mostly late game is about making your character look cool. Also, picking a race will affect your personal story, but none have any in-game advantage over the others.

Leveling is mostly done through events that just happen in the world. You're never going to have a list of quests that you need to complete; just wander around and do what looks interesting. If an area is too easy, just head to a different area.

The combat is a lot of fun. There's a lot to learn, but each profession has unique mechanics, and the weapons you pick determine what attacks you will have. There's also a dodging mechanic that you have control over, and a big part of combat is learning when to attack and when to move out of the way so you don't get destroyed.

Everything gives you experience points. Chopping down trees, reviving other players (oh, yeah, everyone can revive everyone else), crafting, just exploring the maps, and the usual killing stuff and completing events.

There's probably more, but it's hard to think of everything.
